relationship: A single linear scale factor changes corresponding lengths by that factor, areas by its square and volumes by its cube.
rationale: The canonical lesson keeps one manipulable solid and one model-led sequence: observe a length change, count the corresponding face and volume changes, then reverse the relationship and test similarity.

learnerLoop.action: Resize the production solid, compare observations and complete the scale-factor chain.
learnerLoop.modelChange: All solid edges, layers, area and volume values update from one scale factor.
learnerLoop.evidence: The linked solids, unit layers, recorded trials and calculation chain show the powers of scale.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Use the observed linear factor to predict or explain the area and volume factor.

invariants: Similar solids keep one common linear scale factor across corresponding edges.
Area and volume factors are respectively the square and cube of that factor.
A geometry change invalidates earlier working checks and target calculations.
safeAdaptations: Vary positive scale factors and prototype dimensions.
Adjust working support while preserving the linked length, area and volume representations.
Offer a sparse fresh target calculation after the guided sequence without adding a separate dashboard.
nonGoals: Applying the linear scale factor directly to area or volume.
Adding an unrelated formula catalogue or a second model.

task.description: Current scale problem, target and concise working prompt.
task.visibility: Shown for the current guided stage or experiment target.

model.description: The linked reference and scaled solid, with unit layers and annotations that update from the same scale factor.
model.visibility: Present throughout; model controls follow the current stage.

working.description: Short scale, area, volume or target-calculation entries tied to the current model.
working.visibility: Shown when the current stage needs learner calculation.

evidence.description: Annotations, recorded readings and optional comparison preserve the same dimensions and factors.
evidence.visibility: Updates during resizing and after a recorded experiment reading.

completion.description: Feedback and guided continuation after the current manipulation and working conditions are met.
completion.visibility: Persistent dock with completion state supplied by the shared runtime.

inputs.description: Scale or height handles, calculation entries and the small set of experiment controls.
inputs.visibility: Generated for the active stage; the optional target field appears only after New target.

linear-scale.description: Common edge scale from the reference solid to the production solid.
linear-scale.domain: Positive scale factor k and corresponding edge length.
linear-scale.source: Generated scale target and #stage model control.
linear-scale.output: Solid dimensions, edge annotation and k in the working/evidence surfaces.

area-factor.description: Corresponding face-area factor k² and face values.
area-factor.domain: Square units and square scale factor.
area-factor.source: Computed from the common linear scale.
area-factor.output: Face annotation and area working entry.

volume-factor.description: Solid-volume factor k³ and corresponding volume values.
volume-factor.domain: Cubic units and cube scale factor.
volume-factor.source: Computed from the common linear scale and layer count.
volume-factor.output: Volume annotation and volume working entry.

target-check.description: Optional checked area or volume factor for a fresh experiment target.
target-check.domain: Positive factor matched to the generated target kind.
target-check.source: New target selects a bounded area or volume target from the same model.
target-check.output: Checked target state before the reading can be recorded.

counterexample.description: A one-dimension stretch used to show unequal ratios and loss of similarity.
counterexample.domain: Corresponding edge ratios in the test-condition stage.
counterexample.output: Linked edge annotations and feedback on #stage.

modes.none: The guided source stages show the manipulated edge, face and volume evidence before requiring prediction.
modes.some: Intermediate stages ask for the linear factor or a concise prediction while the model supplies linked measurements.
modes.all: Later guided stages require the relevant factor, resize and test conditions before continuation.
modes.experiment: The final stage keeps Separate layers, Record reading and New target; a target calculation is checked only when a fresh target is requested.

dependencies: The same scale factor drives every displayed length, area and volume quantity.
A target or geometry change clears the associated working check before feedback can mark the stage complete.
The one-dimension stretch must be repaired before the similarity-condition stage can complete.
Recorded readings are derived from the current model and comparisons retain their recorded dimensions.
implementation.completion: The shared runtime advances after the current model condition, required calculation and any experiment target check agree; the final experiment remains bounded by the existing guided controls.
limitations: The optional target field is intentionally sparse and appears only after New target.
Separate layers is a visual representation action and does not add an answer quantity.
